name: Pixel UI as a living screencast
look: a real hi-res interface with a low-res pixel mascot living and acting inside it.

products: anything whose agent can be a mascot
fits.notes: dev tools, agents, automations (the mascot IS the agent)

when_not: Avoid if the mascot is not the product's agent; no random sprite quota.

type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: product's real UI type; mascot in a 5-colour palette from the brand.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: mascot palette is 5 colours drawn from the brand
brand_lock.type_role: the product's real UI type, unchanged
brand_lock.world_changes: a hi-res real interface with a low-res pixel mascot acting inside it
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

hints: mascot hops between real buttons, "eats" a log line, carries a card
the mascot's resolution is the contrast
motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects.role: on the mascot canvas only; the real UI plate stays hi-res

effects_note: rasan-fx passes (runtime/rasan-fx.js); order is the pass order. {brand_colour} / {second_ink} are filled from the brand or look palette.

codex_assets.prompt_template: sprite sheet of {mascot}: idle, walk, carry, celebrate, equal 4x4 grid, 5-colour brand-derived palette, flat pure chroma-green (#00FF00) background, equal cells with even gutters, no text, no labels
codex_assets.r1_note: sprite sheet of the mascot (idle, walk, carry, celebrate), A4.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

palette: tiny UI ticks plus soft pixel chirps per action

build.engine_meaning: buildable today / reference only (builder hand-codes it)
build.recipe: style `living-screencast.md`; `medium-pixel-companion.js`; DOM UI plate + canvas sprite on top.

examples.title: lemo-opuscar `living-screencast` (in repo, third_party); Duolingo's mascot-in-UI work

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.

palettes.name: Paper desk
palettes.words: warm paper white, soft black, vermilion, cobalt

palettes.name: Night shift
palettes.words: ink violet, lilac white, bubblegum pink, cyan

brand_lock.rule: The real UI keeps its own palette untouched. Brand colour tints the mascot's one signature item (scarf, visor); background and ink are style-fixed and match the UI's host surface. Slots marked brand take the brand colour (exact hex); slots marked style keep the palette value; brand-or-style takes the brand colour only when its contrast against the other slot is at least 4.5:1, else the palette value.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

pairings.note: Pixel type only for the mascot's speech bubble; everything else is the product's own UI type.

scale.note: cqw = 1% of the frame width (1080p: 1cqw = 19.2 px)

type.load: In a HyperFrames composition add the two <link> tags from `google` to <head> (plus rel=preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com), set font-family from `css`, and wait for document.fonts.ready before the first screenshot / timeline build. Offline renders: download the families once (they are OFL) into the project's fonts/ folder and use @font-face. The brand face always sets the real claim line and the product UI text; the style pairing is for the world's chrome and display.
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text. Under a brand lock keep the brand face for the claim and use the pairing's display for labels only.

passes.role: mascot layer only, never the UI capture

finish.how: Runtime: RasanFX.create({ source, passes: [...] }) from runtime/rasan-fx.js, applied in the listed order, on the whole composition canvas or on the Codex plate only (plate-only when the type must stay crisp). `css` lists the cheap approximation kinds story boards and style frames draw with plain CSS (grain:<opacity>, scan:<opacity>, halftone, pixel, led-dots ...).

composition.grid: the real UI capture is the stage; the mascot is a 32-64 px-tall sprite layer on 3x integer steps
composition.safe_area: UI keeps its own margins; mascot walks along real element edges (button tops, card borders)
composition.fill: UI fills 85-95% of the frame; mascot under 8% of the area
composition.product_ui: UI is the world itself: do not frame it in a device, composite the sprite directly on the capture

codex.template: {subject} {action}, {setting}. Camera and lens: flat orthographic screen-aligned view of a sprite on a transparent or flat chroma-green ground. Lighting: flat; a 1 px darker underside only. Material: hard-edged pixel sprite, 1 px dark outline, 6-10 colours, no anti-aliasing. Colour, locked to the palette {palette_words}, and nothing outside it. Texture and finish: none; no dither on the sprite except 2 shading steps. Avoid: no text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no UI screenshot, no scene background, no anti-aliasing, no glow, no text in the speech bubble.
codex.camera: flat orthographic screen-aligned view of a sprite on a transparent or flat chroma-green ground
codex.lighting: flat; a 1 px darker underside only
codex.material: hard-edged pixel sprite, 1 px dark outline, 6-10 colours, no anti-aliasing
codex.colour_rule: Name the palette's colours in words (the palette's `words`), never hex codes; add 'and nothing outside this palette'. Pick one palette per film and keep it.
codex.texture: none; no dither on the sprite except 2 shading steps
negatives: no text in the speech bubble

aspect.note: Plates: ask for about 12% bleed around the frame so the camera can travel; keep the calm side empty for type. Generate 16:9 for the frame, 1:1 for sprite sheets and objects.

consistency.anchor: Make the anchor plate first, approve it by eye, then pass it as --ref to every other image (imagegen batch does this with --world).
consistency.style_line: Append the world bible's style line (30-45 words, no hex) to every prompt.
consistency.seed_words: Keep these words verbatim in every prompt of the film: hard-edged pixel sprite; flat orthographic screen-aligned view of a sprite on a transparent or flat chroma-green ground; near-black graphite, off-white, mint, amber.

sprite_sheet.rules: Sprite sheet: flat chroma-green background (#00FF00) that fills the whole sheet, an equal grid of cells with identical size and spacing, one pose or state per cell, same ground line and scale in every cell, no text, labels, numbers or grid lines, no green anywhere in the sprite (if the chosen palette contains green, use another palette for sprites). Cut out with --transparent, snap to the palette afterwards.

do: One mascot, one job in the story, consistent 3x scale
Let the sprite touch real UI geometry (stand on a button, push a toggle)
Snap sprite positions to the pixel grid
dont: Do not redraw or pixelate the real UI
Do not add random decorative sprites
Do not smooth sprite motion between pixel steps
cheap_ways: Mascot floats over the UI without touching any edge
Sprite scaled to 2.5x so pixels differ from the UI's own 1x
